questions.stem:
The number of candidates (in lakhs) who appeared in an examination from four different cities, and the ratio of passed to failed candidates within each city:

| City | $C_1$ | $C_2$ | $C_3$ | $C_4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of candidates (in lakhs) | 3.14 | 1.25 | 2.27 | 1.08 |
| Ratio of passed : failed | 5 : 3 | 7 : 3 | 1 : 3 | 4 : 5 |

Which city has the highest number of candidates failed in the examination?
questions.explanation:
Apply each failure ratio to that city's candidate count:

| City | Failed share | Failed (lakhs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $C_1$ | $3/8$ of 3.14 | 1.18 |
| $C_2$ | $3/10$ of 1.25 | 0.38 |
| **$C_3$** | $3/4$ of 2.27 | **1.70** |
| $C_4$ | $5/9$ of 1.08 | 0.60 |

$C_3$ has the most failures — note that $C_1$ has more candidates overall, but $C_3$'s far worse pass ratio outweighs that.

questions.stem:
The number of candidates (in lakhs) who appeared in an examination from four different cities, and the ratio of passed to failed candidates within each city:

| City | $C_1$ | $C_2$ | $C_3$ | $C_4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of candidates (in lakhs) | 3.14 | 1.25 | 2.27 | 1.08 |
| Ratio of passed : failed | 5 : 3 | 7 : 3 | 1 : 3 | 4 : 5 |

Which city has less than fifty thousand failed candidates in the examination?
questions.explanation:
Fifty thousand is **0.5 lakh**, so compare each city's failures against 0.5:

$$C_1: 1.18,\quad \mathbf{C_2: 0.375},\quad C_3: 1.70,\quad C_4: 0.60.$$

Only $C_2$ falls below 0.5 lakh. $C_4$ is the near miss at 0.6 lakh.

questions.stem:
The number of candidates (in lakhs) who appeared in an examination from four different cities, and the ratio of passed to failed candidates within each city:

| City | $C_1$ | $C_2$ | $C_3$ | $C_4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of candidates (in lakhs) | 3.14 | 1.25 | 2.27 | 1.08 |
| Ratio of passed : failed | 5 : 3 | 7 : 3 | 1 : 3 | 4 : 5 |

Which cities individually have more than 50% pass percentage?
questions.explanation:
A pass ratio beats 50% exactly when the passed part of the ratio exceeds the failed part:

$$C_1 = \tfrac58 = 62.5\%\ \checkmark,\quad C_2 = \tfrac7{10} = 70\%\ \checkmark,\quad C_3 = \tfrac14 = 25\%,\quad C_4 = \tfrac49 = 44.4\%.$$

So **$C_1$ and $C_2$** — and note the candidate counts are irrelevant here, only the ratios matter.

questions.stem:
The number of candidates (in lakhs) who appeared in an examination from four different cities, and the ratio of passed to failed candidates within each city:

| City | $C_1$ | $C_2$ | $C_3$ | $C_4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number of candidates (in lakhs) | 3.14 | 1.25 | 2.27 | 1.08 |
| Ratio of passed : failed | 5 : 3 | 7 : 3 | 1 : 3 | 4 : 5 |

The average pass percentage over all cities in the examination is approximately ________.
questions.explanation:
This is a **weighted** figure — total passed divided by total appeared, not the mean of the four percentages.

**Total appeared:** $3.14 + 1.25 + 2.27 + 1.08 = 7.74$ lakh.

**Total passed:**
$$\tfrac58(3.14) + \tfrac7{10}(1.25) + \tfrac14(2.27) + \tfrac49(1.08) = 1.963 + 0.875 + 0.568 + 0.480 = 3.885.$$

$$\frac{3.885}{7.74} \times 100 \approx 50\%.$$

*(Averaging the four percentages instead gives about 50.5% — close here, but the weighted method is the correct one.)*

A pie chart gives the monthly expenditure of a household under various heads, as sector angles:

| Head | Sector angle |
| --- | --- |
| Food | $80^\circ$ |
| Children Education | $70^\circ$ |
| House Rent | $55^\circ$ |
| Travel | $45^\circ$ |
| Savings | $40^\circ$ |
| Miscellaneous | $40^\circ$ |
| Electricity | $30^\circ$ |

If the amount spent on electricity in a month is Rs. 8,100, the amount saved in the month in rupees is
questions.explanation:
Angles are proportional to amounts, so first find the value of one degree:
$$\frac{8100}{30^\circ} = 270 \text{ rupees per degree}.$$

Savings occupy $40^\circ$:
$$40 \times 270 = \text{Rs. } 10{,}800.$$

*(Shortcut: savings and electricity are in the ratio $40:30 = 4:3$, so savings $= \frac43 \times 8100$.)*

questions.stem:
A pie chart gives the monthly expenditure of a household under various heads, as sector angles:

| Head | Sector angle |
| --- | --- |
| Food | $80^\circ$ |
| Children Education | $70^\circ$ |
| House Rent | $55^\circ$ |
| Travel | $45^\circ$ |
| Savings | $40^\circ$ |
| Miscellaneous | $40^\circ$ |
| Electricity | $30^\circ$ |

The amount spent on children education in a month is what percent of the amount spent on food in that month?
questions.explanation:
Since both amounts scale with their angles, the ratio of angles is the ratio of amounts:
$$\frac{70^\circ}{80^\circ} \times 100 = 87.5\%.$$

The household total never enters the calculation.

questions.stem:
A pie chart gives the monthly expenditure of a household under various heads, as sector angles:

| Head | Sector angle |
| --- | --- |
| Food | $80^\circ$ |
| Children Education | $70^\circ$ |
| House Rent | $55^\circ$ |
| Travel | $45^\circ$ |
| Savings | $40^\circ$ |
| Miscellaneous | $40^\circ$ |
| Electricity | $30^\circ$ |

In a month, savings is what percent of the total expenditure?
questions.explanation:
A full pie is $360^\circ$, and savings take $40^\circ$:
$$\frac{40}{360} \times 100 = \frac{100}{9} = 11\tfrac19\%.$$
